title: Pharmacological profile of a novel, non-TZD PPARgamma agonist.
text_summary: 本文发表于Diabetes, Obesity & Metabolism（2005，IF=5.4），评价一种新型非噻唑烷二酮类PPARγ激动剂RWJ-348260的药理学特征。体外实验通过PPARγ-GAL4转染、受体结合、aP2基因诱导和前脂肪细胞分化试验证实该化合物可选择性激活PPARγ。研究随后在ob/ob小鼠、db/db小鼠和Zucker糖尿病肥胖大鼠中进行多日口服给药，结果显示RWJ-348260可显著降低血糖、HbA1c、胰岛素和三酰甘油，改善口服葡萄糖耐量，并在白色脂肪组织中上调PPARγ靶基因。与罗格列酮相比，该药在维持降糖和调脂疗效的同时，引起的肝细胞脂质沉积、肝重增加、血液稀释及体重增加较少，且未明显影响转氨酶、胆红素和血细胞比容。作者认为RWJ-348260具有有效的抗糖尿病作用和较优的副作用特征，可作为2型糖尿病及胰岛素抵抗治疗的候选PPARγ激动剂。

Pharmacological profile of a novel, non-TZD PPAR g agonist
X. Chen, M. C. Osborne, P. J. Rybczynski, R. Zeck, M. Yang, J. Xu, L. Zhou, E. Cryan,
Y. Tang and K. T. Demarest
Endocrine Therapeutics and Metabolic Disorders Team, Drug Discovery, Johnson & Johnson Pharmaceutical Research and
Development, L.L.C., Raritan, NJ, USA
Aim: The purpose of this study was to characterize a novel, non-thiazolidinedione (TZD) peroxisome proliferator-
activated receptor (PPAR) g agonist, RWJ-348260, via both in vitro and in vivo approaches.
Methods: The in vitro PPARg activities of RWJ-348260 were assessed in PPAR g-GAL4 co-transfection assay, PPAR g
receptor binding assay, aP2 gene induction assay and preadipocyte differentiation assay. The in vivo efficacy of the
compound was determined in rodent genetic diabetes models [ ob/ob mouse, db/db mouse and Zucker diabetic fatty
(ZDF) rat] following multiple days of oral administration.
Results: RWJ-348260 selectively activated PPAR g in vitro. In vivo , RWJ-348260 produced significant decreases in
plasma glucose, HbA1c, insulin and triglyceride levels. RWJ-348260 also dose-dependently improved oral glucose
tolerance. In db/db mice, the compound up-regulated PPAR g target genes in white adipose tissues. RWJ-348260
produced a lower extent of hepatocyte lipid deposition and a smaller increase in liver weight compared to rosiglita-
zone in db/db mice. While RWJ-348260 effectively normalized hyperglycaemia and dyslipidaemia, it did not change
haematocrit, transaminase, alkaline phosphatase, total bilirubin levels or liver weights in ZDF rats.
Conclusions: RWJ-348260 is a potent PPAR g agonist with efficacious antidiabetic activity in diabetic animal models.
The compound has an improved side-effect profile compared to rosiglitazone.
Keywords: PPAR g, antidiabetic drugs, glycaemic control, HbA1c, OGTT, haematocrit

Introduction
Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors (PPARs) are
members of the nuclear hormone receptor superfamily,
including three receptor isoforms, PPAR a, PPAR g and
PPARd[1–4]. These receptors are ligand-activated tran-
scription factors that modulate the expression of various
target genes and play a central role in maintaining glu-
cose and lipid homeostasis. Several therapeutic agents
used in the treatment of type 2 diabetes and dyslipidae-
mia are ligands for PPAR g and PPAR a, respectively [5].
The PPAR g receptor is considered to play a key role in
adipogenesis [6,7]. Before naturally occurring ligands
were identified for PPAR g, it was demonstrated that a
class of antidiabetic agents known as thiazolidinediones
(TZDs) were high affinity PPAR g ligands [8–10]. TZDs
enhance insulin sensitivity by binding to the PPAR g
receptor in adipocytes (primarily), liver and skeletal
muscle, stimulating peripheral glucose uptake and util-
ization [11–13]. A growing body of evidence indicates
that the beneficial effects of PPAR g agonists on metab-
olism may be mediated by the following: enhanced insu-
lin-sensitive uptake and storage of free fatty acids in

adipose tissue [14]; increased production of adiponec-
tin, a secreted adipocyte-specific protein with potential
insulin-sensitizing activity [15–17]; and inhibited
expression of tumour necrosis factor alpha (TNF a)
[18,19], resistin [20], 11 b-HSD-1 [21] and other proteins/
enzymes mediating insulin resistance.
RWJ-348260 is an orally active PPAR g agonist. The
compound has novel structural features (figure 1) com-
pared to other PPAR g agonists reported previously [22].
For instance, the TZD ring has been replaced with a
carboxylic acid. The position of the acid is unique,
because it is adjacent to the ether that links to the
remainder of the molecule. The molecule also bears a
fatty side chain on the benzoxazinone ring. This mol-
ecule was investigated in the context of a program in
PPARg agonists, and is considerably different from the
fore-runner compound, MCC-555 [23]. The purpose of
this study was to investigate the in vitro PPARg activity
of RWJ-348260 and evaluate in vivo efficacy of this com-
pound in three genetic animal models, the diabetic db/
db mouse, obese and insulin resistant ob/ob mouse and
Zucker diabetic fatty (ZDF) rat. Rosiglitazone was used
as a comparator in some studies.
Materials and Methods
Human PPARs-GAL4 Reporter Assay
HEK293 cells were cultured and co-transfection assays
were performed as previously described [1] with modifi-
cations. Briefly, the ligand-binding domains of hPPAR a,
g and d were inserted into PM vector (BD Biosciences-
Clontech Inc., Palo Alto, CA, USA) to make hPPAR a-,
g-a n dd-GAL4, respectively. Co-transfection was performed
using DMRIE-C Reagent (Life Technologies, Inc., Rockville,
MD, USA) according to the manufacturer’s instruction.
On the following day, the cells were challenged by adding
5 ml of 20-fold drug solutions (for final concentrations of
3n M to 3 mM) and incubated for 24 h. Luciferase assay was
conducted by using Luciferase Assay System (Promega,
Madison, WI, USA) following the manufacturer’s protocol.
The assay solution were then transferred into DYNEX
Microlite plate (Franklin, MA, USA) and read in the
DYNEX luminometer (Franklin).
PPARg Receptor Binding Assay
Human PPAR g2 cDNA was cloned into expression vec-
tor pET30a (Invitrogen, Carlsbad, CA, USA). His-tagged
recombinant PPAR protein was purified following the
manufacturer’s instructions. Ligand binding assay was
performed using purified recombinant human PPAR g2
protein and radioligand [ 3H] RWJ-348260 (1 mCi/ml,
35 mM, Johnson & Johnson PRD, Spring House, PA,
USA). The assay was set up in a 96-well plate in a total
volume of 150 ml/well TEGM buffer (10 m M Tris–HCl,
pH 7.2, 1 mM EDTA, 10% glycerol, 10 mM sodium molyb-
date). For [ 3H] RWJ-348260 saturation binding assay, a
concentration range of 10–500 n M was used. For com-
pound competition assay, 200 n M of [ 3H] RWJ-348260
was used. Non-specific binding was determined in the
presence of 80 mM cold RWJ-348260 (Johnson & Johnson
PRD, Raritan, NJ, USA). MCC555 (Johnson & Johnson
PRD), rosiglitazone and pioglitazone were used as
comparators. The reaction was carried out at 4 /C14 C over-
night. Then 20 ml of human gamma-globulin (25 mg/ml
in Tris–EDTA, pH 8) and 55 ml 40% PEG8000 (in Tris–
EDTA, pH 8) was sequentially added to each well, mixed
thoroughly and then the incubation continued at room
temperature for 30–45 min. The reaction mixture was
harvested by filtering through a 96-well GF/C filter
plate, followed by several washes with 10% PEG8000.
The filter plate was dried and 30 ml microscintillation
fluid added to each well. The plate was sealed and
counted on Topcount (Packard, Downers Grove, IL,
USA) for [ 3H].
Induction of aP2 Gene Expression in Human
Preadipocytes
AP2 gene induction was measured using branch DNA
(bDNA) technique as previously described [24] with
modifications. The bDNA assay was performed after
24-h treatment of cells with vehicle (DMSO), RWJ-
348260 or rosiglitazone (standard) according to the

Human Preadipocyte Differentiation Assay
Human preadipocytes were purchased from Zen-Bio,
(Research Triangle Park, NC, USA). Cell maintenance
and differentiation procedures were performed accord-
ing to the manufacturer’s instructions with modifica-
tions. Briefly, upon the initiation of the differentiation
assay, preadipocytes were incubated in adipocyte med-
ium (Zen-Bio, catalogue no. AM-1) supplemented with
IBMX (0.5 m M). The medium also contained vehicle
(DMSO), RWJ-348260 or rosiglitazone (standard). A con-
centration range of 0.003–10 mM of each drug was used.
After 3-day incubation, the cell medium was replaced
with the adipocyte medium without IBMX. Eight days
after vehicle or drug treatment, the media was removed
and the cells were fixed with formalin (7% formalde-
hyde in PBS). Total lipid content was determined by
staining with a BODIPY dye (Eugene, OR, USA). Fluor-
escence was quantified using a fluorometric imaging
plate reader (Molecular Devices, Sunnyvale, CA, USA).
Animals Studies
Animals
Female db/db mice and female ob/ob mice (Jackson
Laboratories, Bar Harbor, ME, USA), about 7 weeks of
age when a study was initiated, were fed a certified NIH
Rat and Mouse/Auto 6F diet no. 5K52 (PMI Nutrition
Int’l, St. Louis, MO, USA). Male ZDF/Gmi-Fa rats or
lean control rats (Genetic Models, Indianapolis, IN, USA),
6–7 weeks of age when a study was initiated, were fed
LabDiet 5008 breeding formula (PMI Nutrition Int’l,
St. Louis, MO, USA). Food and water were supplied ad
libitum. Room temperature was maintained at 68–72 /C14 F
and humidity at 50–65%. Room lighting was on a 12-h
light/12-h dark cycle. All of the procedures for animal
studies were approved by the J&J Institutional Animal
Care and Use Committee.
In Vivo Experiments
All drugs were prepared as suspensions in 0.5% hydro-
xypropylmethylcellulose (Dow Chemical, Midland, MI,
USA) in dH 2O (vehicle). Animals were treated with
vehicle or drugs once daily by oral gavage at indicated
doses. Twenty-four hours after the final dose after cer-
tain days of treatment, the animals were bled by retro-
orbital sinus puncture [25]. The livers of some animals
were examined grossly and weighed fresh. For morpho-
logical study, liver tissues were collected and fixed in
10% neutral buffered formalin. For gene expression analy-
sis, subcutaneous white adipose tissues were collected
and frozen into liquid nitrogen immediately. Blood
chemistry analysis and oral glucose tolerance test
(OGTT) were described previously [25].
Morphological Examination of Liver Lipid Deposition
Frozen sections of liver (fixed in formalin) were stained
with oil red O to detect lipid. The oil red O stained livers
were evaluated for the extent of lipid deposition within
hepatocytes while blinded as to treatment groups. The
extent of lipid deposition was scored from 1 to 5 accord-
ing to a criteria as following: 0 ¼ no staining, 1 ¼ trace or
weak staining, 2 ¼ less than 50% of staining, 3 ¼ 50–75%
of staining with higher percentage of weak staining,
4 ¼ generally 50–75% of staining and 5 ¼ greater than
75% of staining.
Quantification of Target Gene Expression from Animal
Tissues by Real-time RT-PCR
RNA was purified from mouse subcutaneous white
adipose tissue (n ¼ 4) following manufacturer’s protocol
(Trizon method, Invitrogen Inc., CA, USA). The cDNA
sequences of mouse malic enzyme (ME), ketoacyl-
Coenzyme A thiolase (KACT), long chain fatty acyl-
Co enzyme A synthase C (ACS-C) and glycerol kinase
(GyK), were obtained from GenBank (accession numbers
are NM_008615, XM_131951, U15977 and NM_008194,
respectively). The polymerase chain reaction (PCR)
primers and fluorescent probes (TagMan probes) were
designed using the software PRIMERDESIGN (Applied Biosys-
tems, Foster City, CA, USA). The primer sequences for ME
are: forward, 5-AAGATTGTGC AAGATGCATA CAAAG;
reverse, 5-CATCTGGGAG GAGACAAATT CTTCT; Taq-
Man probe sequence, 6FAM-TGGCCACTGT TTATCCT-
GAA CCCCAA. The primer sequences for KACT are:
forward, 5-CTGGGAGCTG GCTTCTCTGA T; reverse,
5-CTGTGGTCAT GGCTTGGTTT G; TaqMan probe
sequence, 6FAM-CAGCTCACAC TGTCACCATG GCTT-
GTATCT C. The primer sequences for GyK are: forward,
5-CCATGCCTGA AACAACTGCA; reverse, 5-AACCGC-
TCCA TTGTGACAGC; TaqMan probe sequence, 6FAM-
TTGGTGTGTG GAGTCTTGAA CCTGAGGATT T. The
primer sequences for ACS-C were reported previously [26].
Reverse transcription (RT) and quantitative real time
PCR were conducted in one step using ‘One-Step
RT-PCR Master Mix Reagent’ kit (Applied Biosystems)

Statistical Analysis
Statistical analysis was performed using the program
Graphpad Prism (Monrovia, CA, USA) with one-way
ANOVA and a Dunnett’s multiple comparison test. EC 50,
Kd and Ki values were determined by non-linear regres-
sion with a sigmoidal fit utilizing Graphpad Prism.
Results
RWJ-348260 Potently Activated Human PPAR g
Receptor in PPAR g -GAL4 Chimera Reporter Assay
Using PPAR a, g and d receptor-GAL4 chimera reporter
assays, the PPAR activities of RWJ-348260 were deter-
mined and compared to a known TZD PPAR g agonist,
rosiglitazone (table 1). RWJ-348260 induced PPAR g
reporter gene transcription with a similar potency
(EC50 of 189 /C6 54 nM) to rosiglitazone (EC 50 of
130 /C6 16 nM). The maximal effect of RWJ-348260 was
88% of rosiglitazone’s (data not shown). RWJ-348260
possessed very weak PPAR a (EC50 of 855 /C6 70 nM) and
PPARd (EC50 of 941 /C6 92 nM) agonist properties.
RWJ-348260 Binds to PPAR g 2 Receptor with Similar
Binding Affinity to Rosiglitazone
We analysed the binding affinity of RWJ-348260 by
using [3H]-labelled RWJ-348260 and purified His-tagged
PPARg2 proteins.[ 3H] RWJ-348260 manifested an
affinity of Kd ¼ 216 /C6 99 nM (n ¼ 2) to His-PPAR g2i n
saturation binding studies (fig. 2). Competition experi-
ments using [ 3H] RWJ-348360 demonstrated the binding
affinities (Ki) of various known PPAR g ligands (table 2).
Rosiglitazone, pioglitazone and MCC555 showed bind-
ing affinities of 242, 1955 and 5070 n M, respectively,
which are consistent with previous reports on these
ligands using different assay approaches [8,9,28,29].
RWJ-348260 Induced aP2 Gene Expression in Human
Preadipocytes and Efficiently Induced Human
Preadipocyte Differentiation
Adipocyte fatty acid binding protein (aP2) is a direct
target gene for agonist-activated PPAR g receptor. The
ability of RWJ-348260 to induce aP2 was assessed in
primary human preadipocytes. AP2 gene expression is
minimal in preadipocytes with vehicle treatment (con-
sidered as 1, data not shown). Both rosiglitazone and

RWJ-348260 dramatically induced aP2 gene expression
with maximal 20-fold increases over vehicle (data
not shown). The EC 50s of rosiglitazone and RWJ-
348260 were 77 /C6 35 nM and 147 /C6 24 nM, respectively
(table 1).
PPARg activity of RWJ-348260 was further examined
in human preadipocyte differentiation assay. There was
no preadipocyte differentiation in vehicle-treated cells
(data not shown). Rosiglitazone and RWJ-348260
efficiently induced the differentiation after 8 days of
treatment with maximal sevenfold increases over
vehicle (for both compounds, data not shown). The
EC50s of rosiglitazone and RWJ-348260 were 45 /C6 4n M
and 43 /C6 3n M, respectively (table 1).
Effects of 11 Days of Treatment With RWJ-348260 on
Plasma Glucose, Triglycerides, Insulin, Adipose PPARg
Target Gene Expression and Hepatocyte Lipid Deposition
in 7–8-week-old Femaledb/db Mice
The first animal model used is the db/db mouse
which lacks the ability to modulate body weight
homeostasis due to a leptin receptor mutation. These
mice develop a severe diabetic condition early in life,
with hyperinsulinaemia (at 10–14 days of age) and
hyperglycaemia (starts at 4–6 weeks of age). This
model is commonly used for evaluation of insulin
sensitizers. RWJ-348260 treatment resulted in pro-
found, dose-dependent reductions in plasma glucose
levels compared to vehicle control group (p < 0.001 at
1–30 mg/kg) in db/db mice following 11 days of oral
administration (table 3). The significant decrease in
plasma glucose had already appeared at 1 mg/kg/day
of RWJ-348260 (651 /C6 85 mg/dl in vehicle vs.
309 /C6 55 mg/dl at 1 mg/kg, p < 0.001). Plasma trigly-
ceride levels were also markedly reduced in a dose-
dependent fashion (p < 0.001 at 1–30 mg/kg/day).
RWJ-348260 at 1 mg/kg/day lowered plasma triglycer-
ide levels by 40% (307 /C6 33 mg/dl in vehicle vs.
180 /C6 1 4 m g / d la t1 m g / k g ,p< 0.001). RWJ-348260 at
a dose of 30 mg/kg/day produced a considerable, but
not statistically significant, decrease in plasma insulin
levels (18.1 /C6 3.5 ng/ml in vehicle vs. 4.2 /C6 0.9 ng/ml
at 30 mg/kg).
Expression of PPAR g target genes in white adipose
tissue from the first four animals of each group were
quantified by RT-PCR technique (table 4). Eleven days
of treatment with RWJ-348260 significantly induced
KACT, ME, GyK and ACS genes by maximal five, three,
2.8- and sevenfolds over vehicle, respectively. However,
RWJ-348260 did not change adiponectin and TNF a gene
expression (data not shown).
Effects of RWJ-348260 and rosiglitazone on hepatocyte
lipid deposition were evaluated and compared in a separ-
ate db/db mouse study after 11 days of treatment. RWJ-
348260 increased hepatocyte lipid deposition at 3
(p < 0.01) and 10 mg/kg/day (p < 0.05) (table 5). By com-
parison, rosiglitazone at all the doses (0.3, 1, 3 and
10 mg/kg) was associated with dramatically increased
hepatocyte lipid deposition (p < 0.001). Liver weights
in the animals treated with rosiglitazone were also
much higher than those with RWJ-348260 at equal
doses (1 and 3 mg/kg, p < 0.001).

Twenty-eight Day Treatment With RWJ-348260
Significantly Decreased Serum Glucose, Insulin,
Triglycerides and Increased HDL In 7–8-week-old
Female ob/ob Mice
ob/ob mice lack leptin due to a defect in the ob gene in
adipose tissues. The ob/ob mice develop remarkable
hyperinsulinaemia and relatively mild hyperglycaemia
at the age of 6 weeks. In contradistinction to db/db mice,
which lost theirb cells at 3–6 months, the disease phase of
ob/ob mice is much longer with peak insulin levels at
8–12 months. Therefore, a 28-day study with RWJ-
348260 in a lower dose range was performed in ob/ob
mice. RWJ-348260 at 0.1, 0.3, 1 and 3 mg/kg/day produced
dose-dependent decreases in serum glucose, insulin and
triglyceride levels compared to the vehicle control group
(table 6). The effects of RWJ-348260 were potent, and
statistically significant changes were observed at 0.1 mg/
kg group for all three parameters (p< 0.01). RWJ-348260 at
a dose of 3 mg/kg also significantly increased serum high
density lipoprotein (HDL) levels (p < 0.001).
Fifty-six Day Treatment With RWJ-348260 Efficiently
Reduced HbA1c Levels and Normalized
Hyperglycaemia and Hypertriglyceridaemia in Male
ZDF Rats

onset (type 2) diabetes. The ZDF rat is a markedly
hyperglycaemic strain of fa/fa rat developing obesity,
severe insulin resistance and impaired glucose toler-
ance. Male ZDF rats begin to develop diabetes at the
age of 7 weeks. The primary purpose of this study was
to examine the effect of prolonged treatment of ZDF rats
with RWJ-348260 on HbA1c levels (an indicator of long-
term glucose metabolism status). Table 7 shows that

(p < 0.01 for all three parameters at all the doses). In
fact, the compound reduced glucose levels by 67% at
all three doses following the first two weeks of treat-
ment, and reduced HbA1c by 30–35% at three doses
after 4 weeks of treatment (data not shown). The effects
were further augmented with the time of treatment. The
maximal effects on glucose and HbA1c were achieved at
the lowest dose of 3 mg/kg at the end of the study. The
compound also dramatically reduced plasma total chol-
esterol levels (p < 0.01 at all the doses). Compared to
rosiglitazone, the triglyceride- and cholesterol-lowering
effects of RWJ-348260 were more potent and more effi-
cacious (p < 0.05 compared to rosiglitazone at equal
doses). Both RWJ-348260 and rosiglitazone significantly
increased body weight following 8 weeks of treatment
(p < 0.01 compared to diabetic vehicle group) (table 7).
However, RWJ-348260 caused less weight gain at 10 and
30 mg/kg than rosiglitazone (p < 0.05, compared to rosi-
glitazone at equal doses). Weights of epididymal fat pads
of these animals were significantly increased by both
compounds (approximately twofold increase by RWJ-
348260 and approximately 2.6-fold increase by rosiglita-
zone) compared to vehicle control (data not shown).
Eleven-day or 14-day treatment with RWJ-348260
produced significant decreases in serum glucose,
triglyceride and free fatty acid levels without altering
haematocrit and liver functions in 8–9-week-old male
ZDF rats
Based on the data generated from the 8-week study in
ZDF rats, the subsequent study was performed using a
lower dose range in order to find the lowest efficacy dose
of RWJ-348260. RWJ-348260 at 0.1, 0.3, 1 or 3 mg/kg/day
was given to male ZDF rats for 11 days. Similar to the
observations made in db/db mice, RWJ-348260 at doses
of 1 and 3 mg/kg produced significant decreases in
serum glucose (p < 0.001) and triglyceride levels
(table 8). Although the triglyceride level in the vehicle
group of ZDF rats was much higher than that in db/db
mice (889 /C6 80 mg/dl in ZDF rats vs. 307 /C6 33 mg/dl in
db/db mice), RWJ-348260 at 1 mg/kg was still able to
lower triglycerides by 40% (p < 0.05). The compound
also significantly reduced serum total cholesterol

RWJ-348260 Improved Oral Glucose Tolerance in Male
ZDF Rats
We further evaluated whether RWJ-348260 could
improve glucose tolerance in diabetic animals. Male
ZDF rats were subject to an OGTT following 15 days of
administration of RWJ-348260 (18 h after the last dose
and 16-h fasting). Thirty minutes after the oral glucose
challenge, the plasma glucose levels of vehicle animals
were dramatically increased (from 124 /C6 1.8 to
342 /C6 32 mg/dl), while plasma glucose in RWJ-348260-
treated ZDF rats were significantly suppressed (to
276 /C6 14 mg/dl at 1 mg/kg, p < 0.05 and to 234 /C6 15 mg/
dl, at 3 mg/kg, p < 0.01) (figure 3). At 60 min, plasma
glucose levels in 3 mg/kg group were still significantly
lower than that of control animals (313 /C6 37 vs.
190 /C6 10 mg/dl, p < 0.01).
Discussion
We have demonstrated that RWJ-348260 selectively acti-
vated PPAR g receptor in vitro. In vivo, RWJ-348260 effi-
caciously reduced glucose, insulin and HbA1c levels in
diabetic animals. It also improved glucose tolerance.
These results indicated that this compound acted as an
insulin sensitizer. In addition to the antidiabetic effect,
a long-term 8-week treatment of ZDF rats with
RWJ-348260 produced further reductions in circulating
triglyceride and cholesterol levels with less weight gain
compared to rosiglitazone at the same doses. The weight
gain was primarily reflected in the increases in adipose
tissues. Weight gain and fluid retention are adverse
effects of TZDs in some patients [30]. Weight gain asso-
ciated with TZD use is most likely multifactorial, reflect-
ing increased body fat and fluid retention [30]. Fluid
retention is expressed primarily as mild haemodilution.

decreases in serum albumin and blood haematocrit
(suggesting presence of haemodilution) with dramatic
weight gain (data not shown). In the present study,
while RWJ-348260 effectively lowered hyperglycaemia,
it did not reduce haematocrit after 14 days of treatment
in ZDF rats, although it still increased body weight.
Besides weight gain, rosiglitazone has been found to
produce moderate to severe fatty liver and hepatomegaly
in rodents (table 5 and our unpublished studies). In the
present study, RWJ-348260 produced a lower degree of
hepatocyte lipid accumulation and a smaller increase
in liver weight compared to rosiglitazone at equal doses
in db/db mice. In ZDF rats, RWJ-348260 did not change
serum levels of transaminases, alkaline phosphatase,
total bilirubin and liver weight following 11 days of
treatment. It should be pointed out that a role of PPAR g
played in hepatic steatosis is controversial. It has been
shown that prolonged treatment of obese and diabetic
mice with TZDs resulted in development of hepatic
steatosis [31]. A recent study reported by Gavrilova and
colleagues [32] have demonstrated that liver PPAR g con-
tributes to development of hepatic steatosis in lipo-
atrophic mice and mice with diet-induced obesity using
the liver-specific PPAR g knockout approach. On the
other hand, it has also been shown that TZDs reduced
hepatic fat in Zucker fatty rats [33] and in patients with
non-alcoholic steatohepatitis [34]. It is possible that fatty
liver induced by PPAR g agonist treatment is a species-
specific phenomenon. However, proper precautions
should be taken because of the fact that these drugs can
cause steatohepatitis in animal models.
Accumulated evidence has shown that TZDs mediate
insulin-sensitizing actions through several possible
mechanisms. Berger and colleagues have reported that
a non-TZD PPAR g partial agonist ameliorated hypergly-
caemia and hyperinsulinaemia in high fat-fed C57BL/6 J
mice [26]. The drug also increased adiponectin gene
expression, and decreased expression of TNF a and lep-
tin in epididymal white adipose tissue. Recent studies
have shown that PPAR g in muscle plays a role in regula-
tion of whole body lipid storage and hepatic insulin
sensitivity using a muscle-specific PPAR g knock-
out approach [35,36]. In our study, RWJ-348260 up-
regulated gene expression of some important enzymes
in the pathways of lipogenesis (ME and GyK) and fatty
acid metabolism (KACT and ACS). Previous reports
have shown that those genes could be induced by
PPARg agonists [37–39]. Induction of genes in lipo-
genesis, fatty acid esterification (ACS) and fatty acid
oxidation (KACT) pathways could decrease fatty acid
release from adipose tissue, increase lipid storage and
eventually reduce circulating free fatty acid levels. It has
been demonstrated that elevated circulating free fatty
acid levels contribute to development of insulin resist-
ance [40]. Our data showed that RWJ-348260 reduced
free fatty acids concomitant with improvement of hyper-
glycaemia in ZDF rats, which is consistent with the
hypothesis that PPARg agonists could reduce circulating
free fatty acids by increasing lipogenesis/fat storage/fatty
acid oxidation and subsequently improve insulin sensi-
tivity. However, we did not detect any change in gene
expression of adiponectin and TNF a in db/db mice
treated with RWJ-348260. This might be a result of
missing peak response when samples were collected,
unstable RNA and/or discrepant gene expression levels
to protein levels.
Although the animal models used in these studies are
extreme insulin resistant phenotypes, they provide an
opportunity for investigation of the endocrine, metabolic
and morphologic changes in diabetes. None of the
species exhibits the full spectrum of functional or
structural damages associated with diabetes in humans,
but each offers an opportunity for investigating certain
malfunctions that are common in diabetic humans. In
conclusion, our studies demonstrate that RWJ-348260
acts as a potent insulin sensitzer with comparable

第5页：报告aP2诱导和脂肪细胞分化结果，并以表格呈现db/db小鼠短期给药后的血糖、三酰甘油、游离脂肪酸及其他代谢变化。

第7页：报告ZDF大鼠长期治疗的血糖、HbA1c、三酰甘油和口服葡萄糖耐量改善，并展示多个剂量组的代谢和组织重量数据。

第10页：完成讨论与结论，强调该化合物具有与罗格列酮相当的代谢疗效及较少的肝脂沉积、体重增加和血液稀释；随后开始参考文献。
第11页：参考文献续页，列出PPAR家族、TZD药理、脂肪细胞分化、动物糖尿病模型及PPARγ激动剂安全性相关研究。
